1	# Agent Note: Content-addressed identity and the composition manifest event
2	
3	Status: proposed
4	
5	English | [中文](2026-09-05-composition-manifest.zh.md)
6	
7	## Problem
8	
9	Every identity in the harness names a slot rather than the bytes in it. A `ComponentId` is "derived from its kind and the owning seam's stable name, never from mount order" ([`dsh-components`](../../../../packages/components/components/README.md)), a skill is addressed by its kebab-case name, a prompt section and a tool by their registered names, a preset by its directory name, and a plugin by its package name. Editing a skill body in place leaves all of those addresses unchanged, so a leaderboard cannot separate the generation before the edit from the generation after it, a rollback has no earlier address to return to, and a decontamination check has nothing to key on — the failure the [four-goal-workflows note](2026-09-05-four-goal-workflows.md) records under its rejected "single mutable knowledge store" alternative and forbids in principle P5.
10	
11	Nothing durable records which components a session had in play. The `request/header` event carries each epoch's assembled system prompt text and tool schemas, which is enough to replay a request and not enough to name what produced it: it carries no component identity, provenance, lineage, or registry layer; a skill body loaded through the `skill` tool reaches the transcript as a tool result and never the header; and a dynamic package mounted through [`tool-cordis`](../../../../packages/extensions/tool-cordis/README.md) that registers no tool is invisible in it. The component registry itself is composition-time state that dies with the process, as [the component-registry seam note](2026-09-01-component-registry-seam.md) states outright.
12	
13	Four consumers are blocked on that gap. [`dsh-scorekeeper`](../../../../packages/improvement/scorekeeper/README.md) ships no `composition_hash`, `component_ids`, or `skills_used` field because no event supplies one. W4 stage 1's invariant — a skill result whose digest is absent from the manifest fails — has no manifest to check against. The trajectory exporter can withhold a held-out environment but cannot tell a curated composition from one an agent mutated mid-session, so a synthesized skill body can reach a training set unannounced. And W4 stage 9's knowledge ledger has no address to mirror its entries against, which is what makes "a ledger entry with no matching manifest occurrence never counts as having been in play" enforceable rather than aspirational.
14	
15	## Proposal
16	
17	**One digest function, one address form.** [`dsh-components`](../../../../packages/components/components/README.md) gains `ComponentDigest` (a `Branded<'ComponentDigest'>` from `dsh-brand`) and two pure functions: `componentDigest(kind, canonical)` returns the lowercase SHA-256 hex of `` `${kind}\n${JSON.stringify(canonical)}` ``, and `componentAddress(id, digest)` returns `` `${id}@${digest}` ``. The kind is inside the hashed bytes so two kinds whose canonical values coincide never share an address. The digest is the full 64 hex characters everywhere it is stored or compared, matching `environmentContentHashes` in [`dsh-environments`](../../../../packages/improvement/environments/README.md); truncating it for a card or a table is a presentation choice that never enters a log or the ledger. `ComponentDescriptor` gains a required `digest: ComponentDigest` and a required `digestBasis: 'content' | 'registration'`.
18	
19	**Each producer owns its canonical value.** The registry ships no per-kind canonicalization for the same reason it ships no kind: each producer declares its `ComponentKindMap` member by declaration merging and exports the pure function that canonicalizes it, so a kind added later needs no change in the registry or in the manifest writer. The table below fixes the canonical value of every kind this note introduces.
20	
21	**The registry becomes layered.** `ComponentRegistry` today is one flat `Map`, so it cannot answer "what does this agent see". It moves to `ScopedLayers` from `dsh-scope`, exactly as [`ctx.tools`](../../../../packages/core/tools/README.md) and [`ctx.skills`](../../../../packages/skill/skill/README.md) already do: `register()` files into the calling context's scope, and `list({ kind, scope })` merges the global layer with the viewing scope's chain, the nearest layer's entry winning a duplicate id. A descriptor read back through a scope carries `layer: 'global' | 'agent'` — `global` when the winning registration sits in the global layer, `agent` when it sits in a layer of that agent's scope chain. A deeper chain still reads as `agent`, because a subagent writes its own manifest into its own session.
22	
23	**The manifest writer reads one registry.** `@deepseek-ai/dsh-components-manifest` at `packages/components/components-manifest/` injects `agents` and `components` and nothing else. On `agent/pre-step` it calls `next()` first, recomputes `ctx.components.list({ scope: agent })` for the calling agent, compares the resulting `compositionSha256` with the last `composition/manifest` event in that session's log, and appends a new event through `agent.session.append()` only when the two differ — the shape [`dsh-budget-policy`](../../../../packages/guard/budget-policy/README.md) already uses to fold and append before a step opens. Recomputing rather than tracking incrementally is what keeps it correct across HMR disposal, a preset mounted after creation, and scope shadowing: the writer holds no subscription state that any of those three orderings could invalidate.
24	
25	**Every other seam reaches the manifest through an adapter.** The one-adapter-per-seam rule [the component-registry note](2026-09-01-component-registry-seam.md) established is what keeps the writer from reading registries it does not own, and each adapter follows its seam's own change notification: `dsh-components-tools` follows `tools/change`, `dsh-components-prompt` follows `system-prompt/change`, `dsh-components-skills` follows `tools/result` for the `skill` tool, `dsh-components-presets` follows the `agent-preset/selected` Cordis event, and the shipped `dsh-components-subagents` already follows `subagent/provider-added` and `subagent/provider-removed`. One seam emits nothing today: the dynamic Cordis runner behind `tool-cordis` reports no change when a package is defined, run, stopped, or removed, so `dsh-cordis-host-runner` gains an unfiltered `cordis/dynamic-changed(agent, pluginId)` Cordis event — `@mode emit`, not scope-filtered, so no scope-scan metadata applies — and `dsh-components-packages` follows it.
26	
27	**A skill is in play once its body is loaded, not once it is listed.** `ctx.skills.list()` returns summaries without bodies, so registering every discoverable skill would need a body load per catalog entry per step and would still address a summary rather than the knowledge. `dsh-skill` therefore exports `skillDigest(definition)` over the loaded definition, the `skill` tool's canonical output value gains a `digest` field (absent from `renderSkillContent`, so the model-facing text is unchanged, and durable in `tool/result`), and `SkillInvocationSource` gains the same field so the user-explicit `/name` injection records it too. `dsh-components-skills` registers a `skill` component from either durable record through `exec.agent.ctx`, never by re-parsing the rendered `<skill_content>` block. Skills that were reachable but never loaded stay out of the manifest; the catalog they came from is already durable as the `skill-catalog` message source.
28	
29	## What each kind hashes
30	
31	| Kind | Canonical value | Basis | Producer |
32	|---|---|---|---|
33	| `skill` | `[name, description, whenToUse ?? null, invocation.modelInvocable, invocation.userInvocable, metadata ?? null, content]` from the loaded `SkillDefinition` | content | `dsh-components-skills`, over `skillDigest()` in `dsh-skill` |
34	| `prompt-section` | `[name, order, complete === true, text]` when `PromptSection.text` is a string; `[name, order, complete === true, null]` when it is a provider evaluated per assembly | content, else registration | `dsh-components-prompt` |
35	| `tool` | the model-facing `ToolSchema` as `ctx.tools.schemas(agent)` projects it: name, description, parameter schema, output schema, in the registry's own field order | content | `dsh-components-tools` |
36	| `preset` | `[id, trust, rows]`, where `rows` is the preset's composition after `include` resolution as `[id, name, config, disabled]` per row, with every `name` that resolves to a path rewritten relative to the preset directory | content | `dsh-components-presets` |
37	| `plugin` | `[packageName, version, patchLayerSha256]`, the version from the resolved package manifest and `patchLayerSha256` the SHA-256 over the ordered `cordis.patch.yml` rows of the bundles in force | content | `dsh-components-packages`, over `ctx.loader.entries()` |
38	| `dynamic-package` | `[pluginId, packageId, hostSource, clientSource]` from `ctx.dynamicCordisRunner.inspectPlugin(agent, pluginId)` | content | `dsh-components-packages` |
39	| `agent-provider` | `[provider]` | registration | `dsh-components-subagents` |
40	
41	A digest never covers the viewing scope, the working directory, a wall-clock time, an absolute path (`SkillDefinition.path`, `SkillResourceBase`'s directory, `AgentPreset.path`), a discovery `source` or `rank`, a provider name, or any value a registry computes per assembly. Two hosts that discovered the same skill under different roots, and the same body re-registered through a different provider, therefore address identically; one byte changed in a skill body, a tool parameter description, a static prompt section, or a preset row moves the digest. A `registration`-basis digest addresses the registration and not the bytes the model saw, which is the honest statement for a section whose text is a function of the assembly; the rendered bytes stay where they already are, in `request/header`.
42	
43	## The `composition/manifest` event
44	
45	`dsh-components-manifest` declaration-merges one member into `SessionEventMap` in `@deepseek-ai/dsh-session/types`. It is **log-only** and carries no `@mode` tag: a session log event has no dispatch mode, it rides the single `session/event` emit, and `gen-persistence-catalog` rejects the tag outright — the repo's `@mode` and payload-`@param` rules govern the Cordis bus event this note adds, not this one. It is **required-on-read**, without the envelope's `ignorable: true` marker, because every consumer below keys a refusal on it: a build that cannot interpret the type would otherwise fold a scoreboard row and write an export line for a session it cannot prove was unquarantined ([the version mechanism](../../implemented/architecture/2026-08-10-session-log-version-mechanism.md)). Its payload fields, each carrying its own JSDoc so [the generated catalog](../../../../docs/persistence-catalog.md) documents them:
46	
47	- `kind: 'composition/manifest'` and `version: 1`, the self-declared payload version the environment stamp also carries.
48	- `reason`: why this manifest was written — `'session-start'`, `'preset-mounted'`, `'skill-loaded'`, `'tools-changed'`, `'prompt-changed'`, or `'package-mounted'`, decided by which kinds changed since the previous manifest.
49	- `presetId`: the preset the agent runs, resolved through `resolveSessionPreset()`; absent when the deployment composes none.
50	- `components`: one entry per component in play, ordered by `id`, each `{ id, digest, kind, provenance, lineage?, layer, digestBasis }`.
51	- `compositionSha256`: SHA-256 over the ordered `id@digest` addresses joined by newlines — the deduplication key and the `composition_hash` the scoreboard row wants.
52	- `dynamicPackagesMounted`: whether any entry has kind `dynamic-package`.
53	- `synthesized`: the ids of every entry whose `provenance` is `synthesized`, in the same order.
54	
55	The four-goal note's sketch lists a `seq` field; the envelope already carries `seq`, so the payload does not repeat it. The first manifest is appended before the session's first `request/header`, because `agent/pre-step` runs before the step assembles its request and the preset has already settled by then — a preset chosen after creation commits `agent-preset/selected` while the session is still blank. Every later change to the set in play produces the next differing manifest at the next step, which is the first step whose model request that change can reach.
56	
57	## Quarantine
58	
59	A session is quarantined when its latest manifest reports `dynamicPackagesMounted` or a non-empty `synthesized`, and equally when its log carries no manifest at all: a session that cannot prove what was in play is exactly as unusable as one that mounted code an agent wrote. `SessionFacts.identity` in [`dsh-scorekeeper`](../../../../packages/improvement/scorekeeper/README.md) gains a `composition` group folded from the latest manifest — `compositionSha256`, the entry count, `presetId`, `dynamicPackagesMounted`, and `synthesized` — plus `skillsUsed`, the `id@digest` addresses of every `skill` entry any manifest of the session named. Its `./invariant` companion gains one relation beside the three it checks today: for every `tool/result` of the `skill` tool carrying a digest, some `composition/manifest` at or before that event's `seq` names a `skill` component with that digest, and a result whose digest appears in no manifest is reported as a record disagreeing with its own log. [`dsh-trajectories`](../../../../packages/improvement/trajectories/README.md) gains `includeQuarantined?: boolean` on `TrajectoryExportRequest` and a `quarantined` count on `TrajectoryExportReport`, symmetric with `includeHeldOut` and `heldOut`: absent, the export refuses every quarantined session and accounts for it in the count rather than dropping it silently. The complementary quarantine — a Harness Engineer proposal that touches an evaluator-owned path — belongs to W1 stage 7 and stays there.
60	
61	## The knowledge ledger
62	
63	`@deepseek-ai/dsh-archive` at `packages/improvement/archive/` (`ctx.archive`) holds the cross-session records over [`ctx.storage.domain`](../../../../packages/storage/storage-domain/README.md), through a `defineDomain` spec whose record schemas are zod, routed to whichever backend the deployment configures. Two tables: `variants`, keyed by the `HarnessVariant` id (base commit plus patch-set hash) with the fields the four-goal note fixes — `parent`, `operator`, `patch`, `scores`, `evaluations[]`, `children[]`, `status`, `proposer`; and `generations`, keyed by `id@digest` with `componentId`, `digest`, `kind`, `provenance`, `lineage` (the parent's address, absent for a root), `evidenceSessions[]`, `results`, and `status`. A mutation mints a new row rather than rewriting one, so a generation's bytes and its address never diverge.
64	
65	`status` is `alive`, `dominated`, `promoted`, or `deprecated`. `alive` is evaluated or newly minted and still eligible for parent sampling; `dominated` lost to another generation of its lineage on every measured cell and stays sampleable and auditable, never deleted, which is the archive semantics the four-goal note's rejected best-only alternative exists to preserve; `promoted` carries the `PromotionDecision` that moved it into curated source; `deprecated` is what the department scoreboard writes once a paired present-versus-absent delta has stayed at or below zero over the configured number of runs. Lineage is stored on both ends — `lineage` on the child for the auditor walking up, `children[]` on the parent for the sampler's `1/(1+children)` weight — and a status change appends a revision rather than removing a row.
66	
67	The ledger's `./invariant` companion owns the manifest-versus-ledger relation, an assertion over mutable data against the authoritative event stream the [package invariant rules](../../../../packages/AGENTS.md) require: for every generation row, each session named in `evidenceSessions` must carry a `composition/manifest` whose `components` hold that exact `id@digest`. A row that names an evidence session with no matching occurrence is reported and never counts as having been in play, so a promotion cannot rest on a session the component was not actually composed into.
68	
69	## Alternatives considered
70	
71	**Derive the manifest from `request/header`.** The header already records the assembled system prompt and every tool schema of each epoch, so a fold over it would need no new event. It is rejected because the header carries rendered text and no identity: provenance, lineage, and layer are absent, a loaded skill body never reaches it, and a dynamic package that registers no tool leaves it unchanged — precisely the three cases the quarantine has to catch.
72	
73	**Keep the registry composition-time only, with no session event.** `ctx.components` is already the inventory, so a consumer could read it live. It is rejected because every consumer here reads persisted logs after the fact — the scorekeeper folds them, the exporter writes from them, the ledger invariant checks against them — and composition-time truth dies with the process.
74	
75	**One manifest per session, written at creation.** A single record would be smaller and simpler to fold. It is rejected because a skill load, a preset switch, and a dynamic mount all change the set mid-session, and a start-of-session record would report a clean composition for exactly the sessions the quarantine exists to flag.
76	
77	**Hash each component's rendered contribution.** Hashing what the model actually received would tie the digest to the bytes in the transcript. It is rejected because rendering depends on the working directory, the wall clock, and the viewing scope, so two identical compositions on two hosts would address differently and decontamination would key on noise; `request/header` already owns the rendered bytes, and the manifest owns identity.
78	
79	**Put the per-kind canonicalization in the manifest writer.** One switch over kinds inside the writer would avoid an adapter per seam. It is rejected because the writer would then have to know every kind, which is the coupling `ComponentKindMap`'s declaration merging removes, and a kind added downstream could not be digested at all.
80	
81	**A monotonic version counter per component instead of a content address.** A `skill@3` label is shorter and human-readable. It is rejected for the reason the four-goal note's "single mutable knowledge store" alternative was: a counter is authored rather than derived, so two hosts that refine the same body disagree on the number, a body restored from an ancestor gets a new number instead of its old address, and no consumer can verify the label against the bytes.
82	
83	**A `components/change` event with an incremental writer.** Mirroring `tools/change` would let the writer maintain the manifest between steps instead of recomputing it. It is rejected because recomputation is one registry read and one hash per step and cannot be wrong, while an incremental writer would have to stay correct across HMR disposal, preset remounts, and scope shadowing; no consumer in this note needs a change notification, so the event is not added until one does.
84	
85	**The ledger as session events rather than storage.** Recording generations in the log would keep everything on one plane. It is rejected because a ledger spans sessions and outlives every one of them, and because the manifest-versus-ledger invariant needs two planes to be a real check: an entry that is itself a session event could not be contradicted by the session events it cites.
86	
87	## Acceptance criteria
88	
89	- A Loader-booted composition at `examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/composition-manifest/` appends one `composition/manifest` before the session's first `request/header`; the event names the preset id, carries one entry per component in play with a `digest`, `provenance`, `layer`, and `digestBasis`, and its `compositionSha256` equals a recomputation from the ordered `id@digest` addresses in the persisted log.
90	- In the same fixture, the agent calls the `skill` tool once; a second manifest follows with `reason: 'skill-loaded'`, one added `skill` entry whose digest equals `skillDigest()` over that body, and a different `compositionSha256`. A step that changes nothing appends no third event.
91	- Two runs of that fixture under different temporary workspace roots and different `DSH_HOME` values produce byte-identical `compositionSha256` values, proving absolute paths, discovery roots, and timestamps are outside every digest.
92	- `examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/composition-manifest-mutation/` runs the same composition twice with one byte of the skill body changed between the runs; exactly one entry's digest differs, `compositionSha256` differs, and every other entry is unchanged.
93	- `examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/composition-manifest-quarantine/` composes `tool-cordis`, defines and runs a dynamic package, and proves the next manifest reports `dynamicPackagesMounted: true` with the package's id in `synthesized`; the trajectory export then withholds that session and counts it as `quarantined`, and the same export with `includeQuarantined` writes it.
94	- A keyless unit test over a synthetic log proves the scorekeeper invariant reports a `skill` tool result whose digest appears in no preceding manifest, and accepts the same result once a manifest names it; a second proves a session with no manifest at all folds to a quarantined record rather than a clean one.
95	- A keyless unit test in `packages/improvement/archive/tests/` proves the ledger invariant reports a generation row whose evidence session carries no manifest occurrence of its `id@digest`, and accepts the row once one exists.
96	- The persisted-log snapshot suite `examples/headless-agent` owns records the manifest events for the scenario that composes the manifest writer; the event is log-only and changes no model-visible text, so the required coverage is the persisted log rather than a transcript re-record ([testing policy](../../../../docs/testing.md)).
97	
98	## Rollout
99	
100	1. `dsh-components`: the `ComponentDigest` brand, `componentDigest()` and `componentAddress()`, the required `digest` and `digestBasis` on `ComponentDescriptor`, and the `ScopedLayers` layering with `list({ kind, scope })` and the derived `layer`. Updates `dsh-components-subagents` and `dsh-command-components`, [`docs/subsystems/components.md`](../../../../docs/subsystems/components.md), and the three package READMEs.
101	2. The composition-time adapters and their canonical values: `dsh-components-tools`, `dsh-components-prompt`, and `dsh-components-presets` at `packages/components/`, each following its seam's existing change event.
102	3. `dsh-components-manifest`: the `composition/manifest` declaration, the `agent/pre-step` writer with `compositionSha256` deduplication, the regenerated `known-event-types.ts` and persistence catalog, and the `composition-manifest` fixture.
103	4. Skill generations: `skillDigest()` in `dsh-skill`, the `digest` field on the `skill` tool's canonical value and on `SkillInvocationSource`, `dsh-components-skills`, and the mutation fixture.
104	5. Dynamic packages: `cordis/dynamic-changed` on `dsh-cordis-host-runner`, `dsh-components-packages` over `ctx.loader.entries()` and the dynamic runner, and the quarantine fixture.
105	6. Quarantine consumers: the `composition` group and `skillsUsed` on `SessionFacts`, the scorekeeper invariant relation, and `includeQuarantined` with the `quarantined` count in `dsh-trajectories`.
106	7. `dsh-archive`: the domain spec, the `variants` and `generations` tables, the four statuses and their transitions, the two-ended lineage edges, and the manifest-versus-ledger invariant.
107	
108	## Risks
109	
110	A `registration`-basis digest cannot detect a change in what a provider-evaluated prompt section produced, so two runs whose dynamic sections differed share an address. `request/header` carries those bytes and a comparison that needs them must read it; a leaderboard keyed on the manifest alone will pool the two.
111	
112	A `plugin` digest keys on package name and version, and every workspace package here is `0.0.1`, so a source edit does not move it. `HarnessVariant`'s base commit plus patch-set hash is what addresses harness source, and a comparison that keys on plugin digests alone will pool generations of the same package.
113	
114	The manifest names components, not their transitive effects. An MCP server whose remote tool descriptions change without a re-registration, or a skill whose body references a file that changed, keeps its digest; only what the canonical value covers is addressed.
115	
116	Required-on-read means a build that does not know `composition/manifest` refuses a log containing it. That is the intended trade — the alternative is a build silently treating a quarantined session as clean — and it is affordable only under the pre-release stance in the root [AGENTS.md](../../../../AGENTS.md).
117	
118	A composition that churns its visible tool set every step writes one manifest per step. Deduplication by `compositionSha256` keeps a stable composition to exactly one event, and a churning one is paying for a real change in what the model can call, but a scoped restriction toggled per step would inflate a log with events no consumer distinguishes.
119

1	# Agent Note: Component registry — every plugin addressable, callable, and scored
2	
3	Status: proposed
4	
5	English | [中文](2026-09-01-component-registry-seam.zh.md)
6	
7	## Problem
8	
9	Model-callable surfaces are per-kind and disjoint. Tools are called through `ctx.tools`, skills through the `skill` tool over `ctx.skills`, agents through the `subagent` tool over `ctx.subagents`, workflows through the `workflow` and `ralph` tools, and MCP servers through `dsh-mcp-client` mounting their tools; context providers, presets, bundles, and knowledge sources have no callable identity at all. No registry enumerates what a composition can do, and no identity spans kinds.
10	
11	Nothing attaches to a plugin across its life. Lineage (which plugin a synthesized plugin derived from), provenance (curated versus synthesized), and evidence (which certificates a session earned while the plugin was in play) have no home, so the per-agent scores the [verification seam](2026-08-29-verification-improvement-oversight-seams.md) folds cannot extend to the plugins those agents used.
12	
13	Runtime self-improvement stops at the session edge. [`tool-cordis`](../../../../packages/extensions/tool-cordis/README.md) lets an agent define and run a plugin in process memory, and its dynamic packages cannot be promoted automatically by design; a synthesized plugin has no route into a shared catalog, so the loop the Hermes Agent runs for skills (write after use, refine in use, curate the core) and the archive the Darwin Gödel Machine keeps for harness rewrites have no substrate here.
14	
15	A fleet of agents is compositions of compositions: a department is a preset composition of agents, and an agent is a composition of tools, skills, and context plugins. Without one addressing scheme across those levels, leaderboards, judge councils, and promotion policies cannot name what they score.
16	
17	## Proposal
18	
19	Add a component registry [capability seam](../../implemented/architecture/2026-06-13-capability-seams.md). A component is one addressable unit of a composition: a plugin, or a plugin-provided member such as a tool, skill, subagent provider, workflow, MCP server, context provider, preset, or composition. The registry records identity, kind, provenance, lineage, membership, and how a model reaches the component; it executes nothing.
20	
21	**Service Definition (`dsh-components`, `ctx.components`).** `ComponentDescriptor` carries a branded `ComponentId`, a `kind` drawn from the merge-extensible `ComponentKindMap` (each producer package declares its kind by declaration merging, so the registry ships no kind of its own), `name`, `description`, the owning package, `provenance` (`curated` or `synthesized`), an optional `lineage` parent id, optional `members` (child component ids, which makes a composition a component), an optional `invoke` pointer (`{ tool, arguments }`: the existing tool a model calls with fixed arguments to reach the component), and kind-specific `detail`. `register()` returns its disposer and rejects a duplicate id loudly; `list(kind?)` and `get(id)` read. Registrations are composition-time effects, not durable session facts.
22	
23	**Producers: one adapter package per seam.** Each adapter mirrors its seam's live registry into components and stays in sync through that seam's own events. `dsh-components-subagents` registers every provider from [`ctx.subagents`](../../../../packages/subagent/subagent/README.md) as an `agent-provider` component, following `subagent/provider-added` and `subagent/provider-removed`. The component carries no `invoke` pointer: the `subagent` tool is mounted per provider under a configurable name and takes no `provider` argument, and the subagent seam does not expose which tool instance is bound to a provider; the route appears when the tools adapter mirrors tool-subagent instances with their provider binding. Later adapters do the same for tools, skills, workflows, MCP servers, LLM providers, context providers, and presets. A preset composition registers as a `composition` component whose `members` are the components it mounts; that is the recursion a fleet needs: department, agent preset, then tools, skills, and context.
24	
25	**Consumers.** `/components` (`dsh-command-components`) renders the inventory grouped by kind with provenance and lineage for humans. A later `component_invoke` tool dispatches a component's `invoke` pointer so a model reaches any kind through one call beside the native tools, and Code Mode collapses that into one binding. The verification, improvement, and oversight seams take component ids as the subject of certificates, scores, and audits: a certificate records which components were in play, so scores fold per component exactly as they fold per agent.
26	
27	**Promotion.** A synthesized component registers with `provenance: 'synthesized'` and `lineage` pointing at the component it derived from, whether a `tool-cordis` dynamic package or an agent-authored skill, and is usable in its own session immediately. It enters a shared catalog only through the improvement seam's promotion: sessions where it was in play produced verification certificates, the environment registry's evaluation passes, and a user approves; the promotion record keeps the lineage so later synthesis may branch from any ancestor rather than only the current best. Nothing in this seam promotes automatically.
28	
29	## Recursion at fleet scale
30	
31	An organisation is a composition of departments; a department is a `composition` component whose members are agent-preset components; an agent preset is a `composition` whose members are tool, skill, context, and model-provider components; every member is a plugin. The same descriptor describes every level, and `invoke` on a composition starts a subagent from that preset. Leaderboards fold certificates per component id at every level, so a department, an agent, a skill, and a tool are scored by the same rule, and judge councils address their subjects by the same ids.
32	
33	## Alternatives considered
34	
35	**Make `ctx.tools` the universal registry.** Tool definitions are model-facing schema surface with scoped visibility layers; components include non-callable kinds and need lineage and provenance. A tool is one kind of component and stays where it is.
36	
37	**Use MCP as the universal bus.** MCP is a process and wire protocol outside the harness authority model; tools reached through it lose in-process approval, sandbox policy, and the logged-request invariant unless re-wrapped. MCP servers are one kind, not the bus.
38	
39	**Per-kind lineage and provenance fields inside each seam.** Five copies of the same fields diverge, and no cross-kind identity exists for scoring and councils.
40	
41	**Promote dynamic packages automatically once their tests pass.** The Darwin Gödel Machine incidents and Anthropic's cheating taxonomy show self-authored tests are gameable; promotion needs certificates, held-out evaluation, and approval.
42	
43	**A knowledge-graph database as the registry.** The registry is composition-time truth mirrored from live seams; durable facts (promotion records, certificates) ride session events and the storage domain rather than a new database.
44	
45	**Register components by hand from every producing package.** Mirroring a seam's own registry through an adapter keeps components in sync with that seam's events and adds no obligation to seams that predate the registry.
46	
47	## Acceptance criteria
48	
49	- `dsh-components` ships the Service Definition and in-process registry; a keyless test proves duplicate ids are rejected and that disposing a registration removes the component.
50	- `dsh-components-subagents` mirrors every provider present at mount and every later `subagent/provider-added` and `subagent/provider-removed` edge, and disposing the adapter removes its components.
51	- `/components` renders the grouped inventory through the command registry and writes no session events.
52	- A composition component lists its members, and `component_invoke` on it starts a subagent from that preset in a Loader-booted composition.
53	- A synthesized component with no certificate and no approval is refused entry to the shared catalog by a test that exercises the promotion path.
54	- Every phase lands keyless snapshot scenarios through runnable examples per the [testing policy](../../../../docs/testing.md).
55	
56	## Rollout
57	
58	1. Registry seam, the subagent-provider adapter, and the `/components` command.
59	2. Adapters for tools, skills, workflows, MCP servers, LLM providers, context providers, and presets; the `composition` kind; the `component_invoke` tool.
60	3. Promotion: synthesized provenance from `tool-cordis` and skill authoring, certificates as component evidence, improvement-seam evaluation, approval, and the lineage archive.
61	
62	## Risks
63	
64	Mirror drift: an adapter that misses a seam event shows a component that no longer exists. Adapters bind to the seam's own events and register through effects, and disposal tests cover both edges.
65	
66	Two callable surfaces: `component_invoke` beside native tools may split model attention. Native tools remain primary; the uniform call serves kinds without a tool of their own, as Code Mode already collapses many schemas into one binding.
67	
68	Identity stability: ids derive from the kind and the seam's own stable name, never from mount order, so a remount produces the same id.
69	
70	Promotion gaming: identical resubmission, format mimicry, and disguised intent apply to plugins as they do to tasks; the promotion path reuses the verification seam's isolation and the oversight seam's cross-lineage judges.
71

1	/**
2	 * Pure types of the component domain: identities, the merge-extensible kind
3	 * map, descriptors, and the invoke pointer, free of host-side imports.
4	 *
5	 * @module @deepseek-ai/dsh-components/types
6	 */
7	
8	import type { Branded } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-brand'
9	
10	/** Identifies one component; derived from its kind and the owning seam's stable name, never from mount order. */
11	export type ComponentId = Branded<'ComponentId'>
12	
13	/**
14	 * Merge-extensible map from component kind to that kind's detail type. Each
15	 * producer package declares its kind by declaration merging; the registry
16	 * itself ships no kind.
17	 */
18	export interface ComponentKindMap {}
19	
20	/** Every declared component kind; `string` while no producer has merged a kind into the program. */
21	export type ComponentKind = [keyof ComponentKindMap] extends [never] ? string : Extract<keyof ComponentKindMap, string>
22	
23	/** Kind-specific detail declared by the kind's producer; `unknown` for kinds outside this program. */
24	export type ComponentDetail<K extends string> = K extends keyof ComponentKindMap ? ComponentKindMap[K] : unknown
25	
26	/** Whether people curated a component or an agent synthesized it. */
27	export type ComponentProvenance = 'curated' | 'synthesized'
28	
29	/** The existing tool a model calls, with fixed arguments, to reach a component. */
30	export interface ComponentInvoke {
31	  /** Registered tool name. */
32	  readonly tool: string
33	  /** Arguments fixed by the component; the model supplies the rest. */
34	  readonly arguments?: Readonly<Record<string, string>>
35	}
36	
37	/** One addressable unit of a composition. */
38	export interface ComponentDescriptor<K extends ComponentKind = ComponentKind> {
39	  /** Stable identity across compositions. */
40	  readonly id: ComponentId
41	  /** Declared kind. */
42	  readonly kind: K
43	  /** Human-readable name. */
44	  readonly name: string
45	  /** What the component does, stated for people and models. */
46	  readonly description: string
47	  /** Package that produced the registration. */
48	  readonly owner: string
49	  /** Curated by people or synthesized by an agent. */
50	  readonly provenance: ComponentProvenance
51	  /** Component this one derived from, absent for roots. */
52	  readonly lineage?: ComponentId
53	  /** Child components of a composition, absent for leaves. */
54	  readonly members?: readonly ComponentId[]
55	  /** How a model reaches the component, absent for kinds without a callable route. */
56	  readonly invoke?: ComponentInvoke
57	  /** Kind-specific detail. */
58	  readonly detail: ComponentDetail<K>
59	}

1	/**
2	 * Component registry: identity, kind, provenance, lineage, membership, and the
3	 * callable route of every addressable unit in a composition. The registry
4	 * executes nothing and holds composition-time state only. The
5	 * [component-registry Agent Note](../../../.agents/notes/proposed/architecture/2026-09-01-component-registry-seam.md)
6	 * owns the design rationale.
7	 * @module @deepseek-ai/dsh-components
8	 */
9	
10	import { Context, Service } from '@deepseek-ai/cordis'
11	import { HarnessError } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm'
12	import type { ComponentDescriptor, ComponentId as ComponentIdType, ComponentKind } from './types.ts'
13	
14	export type * from './types.ts'
15	
16	declare module '@deepseek-ai/cordis' {
17	  interface Context {
18	    components: ComponentRegistry
19	  }
20	}
21	
22	/** Stable error codes for rejected component registrations. */
23	export type ComponentErrorCode = 'COMPONENT_DUPLICATE_ID'
24	
25	/** Error returned by the component registry boundary. */
26	export class ComponentError extends HarnessError {
27	  /**
28	   * @param message - human-readable rejection reason.
29	   * @param code - stable machine-routable classification.
30	   */
31	  // Keep the constructor to narrow HarnessError's string code at this boundary.
32	  // oxlint-disable-next-line typescript/no-useless-constructor -- type-only narrowing
33	  constructor(message: string, code: ComponentErrorCode) {
34	    super(message, code)
35	  }
36	}
37	
38	/**
39	 * Brand a string as a component id.
40	 * @param id - raw component identifier.
41	 * @returns the same string with the compile-time brand.
42	 */
43	export function ComponentId(id: string): ComponentIdType {
44	  return id as ComponentIdType
45	}
46	
47	/** Copy a descriptor so callers never share the registry's stored arrays. */
48	function detach(descriptor: ComponentDescriptor): ComponentDescriptor {
49	  return {
50	    ...descriptor,
51	    ...descriptor.members === undefined ? {} : { members: [...descriptor.members] },
52	  }
53	}
54	
55	/** Component registry (`ctx.components`): the composition-time inventory mirrored from live seams. */
56	export class ComponentRegistry extends Service {
57	  private readonly components = new Map<ComponentIdType, ComponentDescriptor>()
58	
59	  constructor(ctx: Context) {
60	    super(ctx, 'components')
61	  }
62	
63	  /**
64	   * Register one component. Registrations are effects: the producer keeps the
65	   * returned disposer under its own fiber so disposal removes the component.
66	   * @param descriptor - complete component description.
67	   * @returns the exact disposer that removes this registration and no later one under the same id.
68	   * @throws {@link ComponentError} when the id is already registered.
69	   */
70	  register(descriptor: ComponentDescriptor): () => void {
71	    if (this.components.has(descriptor.id)) {
72	      throw new ComponentError(`component "${descriptor.id}" is already registered`, 'COMPONENT_DUPLICATE_ID')
73	    }
74	    const stored = detach(descriptor)
75	    this.components.set(stored.id, stored)
76	    return () => {
77	      if (this.components.get(stored.id) === stored) this.components.delete(stored.id)
78	    }
79	  }
80	
81	  /**
82	   * Read one component.
83	   * @param id - component identity.
84	   * @returns a detached descriptor, or `undefined` when nothing is registered under the id.
85	   */
86	  get(id: ComponentIdType): ComponentDescriptor | undefined {
87	    const stored = this.components.get(id)
88	    return stored === undefined ? undefined : detach(stored)
89	  }
90	
91	  /**
92	   * List components in registration order.
93	   * @param kind - when given, only components of this kind.
94	   * @returns detached descriptors.
95	   */
96	  list(kind?: ComponentKind): ComponentDescriptor[] {
97	    return [...this.components.values()]
98	      .filter(component => kind === undefined || component.kind === kind)
99	      .map(detach)
100	  }
101	}
102	
103	export default ComponentRegistry

# AGENTS.md — Harness Packages

These package-specific rules supplement the repo-wide [conventions](../AGENTS.md#conventions).

- **Plugin exports:** service packages default-export their service class; function plugins named-export `name` / `inject` / `Config` / `apply` and have no default export. Mixing the forms makes the Loader discard the function plugin's namespace ([postmortem](../docs/postmortem/0001-acp-default-export-drops-inject.md)).
- **Optional services use `ctx.get(name)`.** Reserve `ctx.<name>` for declared injections; the property proxy is topology-sensitive, while strict `ctx.get` reads the global service store ([postmortem](../docs/postmortem/0001-acp-default-export-drops-inject.md)).
- **Product-visible plugins require a non-unit REAL-composition test.** Hand-built `ctx.plugin(...)` suites are insufficient. Boot test-only `cordis.yml` through the Loader and app/process; mock only external services or nondeterministic inputs and assert model-visible, durable, or user-visible output. Keep opt-ins out of shipped defaults. [Policy](../docs/testing.md).
- **Initiator-owned private chains derive, then capture.** Under `ctx.agents.withInitiator()`, recover the Agent at each orchestration entry, derive `agent.session`, and let operation-local helpers close over it. Keep `Agent` and `Session` explicit at lifecycle, session-log, service, authority, worker/process, persistence, and wire interfaces; do not widen a leaf helper from `Session` to `Context` merely to hide a parameter ([rationale](../.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-07-15-agent-initiator-scope.md)).
- **Represent one asynchronous operation with one lifecycle controller or transaction.** Separate readiness, cancellation, disposal, reservation, or sentinel state requires an independent owner or settlement point; otherwise fold it while preserving rollback, callback containment, and quiescence.
- **Design Service Definitions for all current Consumers.** Keep tool-schema, Loader, UI, transport, and provider-specific behavior in the Consumer or provider; do not let one Consumer dictate the service contract ([capability-seam rationale](../.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-06-13-capability-seams.md)). Inverse smell: a public service method with one internal caller — pass a private capability closure instead (`RunCodeBridgeOptions`).
- **Require a current owner and need.** Tie each abstraction, state machine, option, defensive copy, and compatibility path to a current contract or production consumer, and keep behavior in its owning plugin or service.
- **Require evidence for public choices.** Configurability does not justify an unsupported default, public operation set, format, or imported external concept. Use current-consumer evidence or relevant prior art; otherwise require an explicit value or defer the choice.
- **Write model-facing contracts from the model's perspective.** Prompts, tool schemas, results, and diagnostics contain only task-relevant concepts, not UI, transport, or implementation vocabulary. Pin stable model-visible text verbatim and dynamic behavior through snapshots or end-to-end coverage.
- **Enforce a decision in the operation that makes it.** Schema omission, prompt filtering, facades, wrappers, and listener order are not enforcement when direct or alternate callers can bypass them; test denial through the executor.
- **Publish state only at its commit point.** Emit each notification and update derived state only after the operation succeeds; derive caches, prompts, UI echoes, replay, and query views from one authoritative source.
- **Apply bounds to the complete result.** Enforce byte, token, item, and time limits where the complete emitted or retained value, including wrappers and metadata, is known; test tiny and exact limits, oversized single chunks, and multibyte byte limits.
- **Registry contributions prove disposal** through the HMR-safety test required by [testing policy](../docs/testing.md): dispose the fiber and observe removal.
- **Every package owns `./invariant`.** Register the manifest name; check an event/data relation or give empty installers package-specific `No runtime invariant:` reasons. Generated companions, unexplained empties, and ignored reporters fail [`verify-package-invariants`](../.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-07-19-package-invariant-runtime-contracts.md).

[Naming rules](../docs/cookbook/adding-a-package.md#name-the-role-that-exists):

- **Package tsconfig:** extends `tsconfig.base.json` (Client: `tsconfig.base.client.json`), uses `rootDir: src`, `outDir: lib/types`, and references each workspace dependency plus `runtime-diagnostics/invariants`; registers in exactly one aggregate. Only `api/remotes` splits for generated contracts; ordinary two-entry Client plugins do not ([layout](../docs/development.md#typescript-project-layout)).
- `src/types.ts` contains only types — no runtime code.
- Tests live at package level under `tests/`, not `src/__tests__/`.
- A package's README and JSDoc are part of the change: altered behavior (config keys, defaults, error codes, wire fields) updates them in the same commit. `doc-sync` gates what it can; apply [dsh-prose-standard](../.agents/skills/dsh-prose-standard/SKILL.md) for complete, concise prose and verify accuracy against code.
- Package READMEs document model, token, and KV-cache effects using the [canonical Model Experience format](../docs/cookbook/adding-a-package.md#4-write-the-package-readme).
- Package READMEs put durable consumer gaps and non-obvious maintainer constraints under `## Known Limitations and Deferred Work`; ordinary cleanup stays in its TODO or Agent Note. Packages with none use a justified [allowlist entry](../scripts/verify-package-readme-limitations.ts) ([rationale](../.agents/notes/implemented/process/2026-07-10-readme-known-limitations-gate.md)).

1	/**
2	 * Mirrors subagent providers into the component registry as `agent-provider`
3	 * components, following the subagent seam's own provider events.
4	 * @module @deepseek-ai/dsh-components-subagents
5	 */
6	
7	import type { Context } from '@deepseek-ai/cordis'
8	import { ComponentId } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-components'
9	import type { ComponentDescriptor, ComponentId as ComponentIdType } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-components/types'
10	// Type-only: resolves ctx.subagents and the subagent lifecycle events.
11	import type {} from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-subagent'
12	
13	export const name = 'components-subagents'
14	export const inject = ['components', 'subagents']
15	
16	/** Kind-specific detail of an `agent-provider` component. */
17	export interface AgentProviderComponentDetail {
18	  /** Provider name as registered with `ctx.subagents`. */
19	  readonly provider: string
20	}
21	
22	declare module '@deepseek-ai/dsh-components/types' {
23	  interface ComponentKindMap {
24	    /**
25	     * One subagent provider registered with `ctx.subagents`. The callable
26	     * route is the `subagent` tool instance configured for the provider; the
27	     * subagent seam does not expose that binding, so the component carries
28	     * no `invoke` pointer.
29	     */
30	    'agent-provider': AgentProviderComponentDetail
31	  }
32	}
33	
34	const OWNER = '@deepseek-ai/dsh-components-subagents'
35	
36	/**
37	 * Component id of one subagent provider.
38	 * @param provider - provider name as registered with `ctx.subagents`.
39	 * @returns the stable id `agent-provider:<provider>`.
40	 */
41	export function agentProviderComponentId(provider: string): ComponentIdType {
42	  return ComponentId(`agent-provider:${provider}`)
43	}
44	
45	/** Describe one provider as a component. */
46	function describeProvider(provider: string): ComponentDescriptor {
47	  return {
48	    id: agentProviderComponentId(provider),
49	    kind: 'agent-provider',
50	    name: provider,
51	    description: `Subagent provider "${provider}", reached through the subagent tool instance configured for it.`,
52	    owner: OWNER,
53	    provenance: 'curated',
54	    detail: { provider },
55	  }
56	}
57	
58	/**
59	 * Register every current provider and follow later additions and removals.
60	 * @param ctx - Cordis context carrying the component registry and the subagent seam.
61	 */
62	export function apply(ctx: Context): void {
63	  const disposers = new Map<string, () => void>()
64	  const add = (provider: string): void => {
65	    if (disposers.has(provider)) return
66	    disposers.set(provider, ctx.components.register(describeProvider(provider)))
67	  }
68	  const remove = (provider: string): void => {
69	    const dispose = disposers.get(provider)
70	    if (dispose === undefined) return
71	    disposers.delete(provider)
72	    dispose()
73	  }
74	  for (const provider of ctx.subagents.list()) add(provider)
75	  ctx.on('subagent/provider-added', (provider) => { add(provider.name) })
76	  ctx.on('subagent/provider-removed', (provider) => { remove(provider) })
77	  ctx.effect(() => () => {
78	    for (const dispose of disposers.values()) dispose()
79	    disposers.clear()
80	  }, 'components-subagents teardown')
81	}

1	/**
2	 * Shared insertion-ordered storage and effect ownership for scope-aware registries.
3	 *
4	 * @module @deepseek-ai/dsh-scope
5	 */
6	
7	import type { Context } from '@deepseek-ai/cordis'
8	import { scopeChainOf, scopeOf } from './index.ts'
9	import type { ScopeKey } from './index.ts'
10	
11	/** One scope's aggregate contribution to a registry. */
12	export interface ScopeLayer {
13	  /** Whether every table in this layer is empty. */
14	  isEmpty(): boolean
15	}
16	
17	/** Internal common read contract for the two entry-table implementations. */
18	interface EntryValues<V> {
19	  values(): IterableIterator<V>
20	  isEmpty(): boolean
21	}
22	
23	/**
24	 * Insertion-ordered named entries with caller-owned duplicate diagnostics.
25	 *
26	 * Values are borrowed. Iterators are live within one nonempty table
27	 * generation; draining the table detaches them from later insertions. Each
28	 * successful insertion returns an idempotent undo for that exact entry.
29	 */
30	export class NamedEntries<V> implements EntryValues<V> {
31	  private data = new Map<string, V>()
32	
33	  constructor(
34	    private readonly duplicateError: (name: string) => Error,
35	  ) {}
36	
37	  /**
38	   * Insert one unique name.
39	   * @param name - name unique within this table.
40	   * @param value - borrowed value to retain.
41	   * @returns an idempotent undo that removes only this insertion.
42	   */
43	  insert(name: string, value: V): () => void {
44	    const data = this.data
45	    if (data.has(name)) throw this.duplicateError(name)
46	    data.set(name, value)
47	    let active = true
48	    return () => {
49	      if (!active) return
50	      active = false
51	      data.delete(name)
52	      if (data.size === 0 && this.data === data) this.data = new Map()
53	    }
54	  }
55	
56	  /**
57	   * Read one named value.
58	   * @param name - name to resolve.
59	   * @returns the retained value, or `undefined` when absent.
60	   */
61	  get(name: string): V | undefined {
62	    return this.data.get(name)
63	  }
64	
65	  /**
66	   * Test one name for membership.
67	   * @param name - name to test.
68	   * @returns whether the table contains that name.
69	   */
70	  has(name: string): boolean {
71	    return this.data.has(name)
72	  }
73	
74	  /**
75	   * Iterate live names in insertion order.
76	   * @returns the native live key iterator.
77	   */
78	  keys(): IterableIterator<string> {
79	    return this.data.keys()
80	  }
81	
82	  /**
83	   * Iterate live entries in insertion order.
84	   * @returns the native live entry iterator.
85	   */
86	  entries(): IterableIterator<[string, V]> {
87	    return this.data.entries()
88	  }
89	
90	  /**
91	   * Iterate live values in insertion order.
92	   * @returns the native live value iterator.
93	   */
94	  values(): IterableIterator<V> {
95	    return this.data.values()
96	  }
97	
98	  /**
99	   * Test whether this table has no entries.
100	   * @returns whether the table is empty.
101	   */
102	  isEmpty(): boolean {
103	    return this.data.size === 0
104	  }
105	}
106	
107	/**
108	 * Insertion-ordered anonymous entries with independent registration identity.
109	 *
110	 * Equal values remain separate registrations. Values are borrowed, and
111	 * iterators are live within one nonempty table generation; draining the table
112	 * detaches them from later appends.
113	 */
114	export class AnonymousEntries<V> implements EntryValues<V> {
115	  private data = new Map<symbol, V>()
116	
117	  /**
118	   * Append one independently owned value.
119	   * @param value - borrowed value to retain.
120	   * @returns an idempotent undo for this exact append.
121	   */
122	  append(value: V): () => void {
123	    const data = this.data
124	    const key = Symbol()
125	    data.set(key, value)
126	    let active = true
127	    return () => {
128	      if (!active) return
129	      active = false
130	      data.delete(key)
131	      if (data.size === 0 && this.data === data) this.data = new Map()
132	    }
133	  }
134	
135	  /**
136	   * Iterate live values in insertion order.
137	   * @returns the native live value iterator.
138	   */
139	  values(): IterableIterator<V> {
140	    return this.data.values()
141	  }
142	
143	  /**
144	   * Test whether this table has no entries.
145	   * @returns whether the table is empty.
146	   */
147	  isEmpty(): boolean {
148	    return this.data.size === 0
149	  }
150	}
151	
152	/**
153	 * Own the global and exact-scope layers for one registry.
154	 *
155	 * Reads never create scoped layers. Registrations derive both visibility and
156	 * effect ownership from the supplied Cordis context, collect undo before
157	 * notification, and reclaim only a completely empty aggregate layer.
158	 */
159	export class ScopedLayers<L extends ScopeLayer> {
160	  /** The eagerly constructed context-global layer. */
161	  readonly global: L
162	
163	  private readonly scoped = new Map<ScopeKey, L>()
164	
165	  constructor(
166	    private readonly createLayer: (scope: ScopeKey | undefined) => L,
167	    private readonly onChange: () => void,
168	  ) {
169	    this.global = createLayer(undefined)
170	  }
171	
172	  /**
173	   * Read an existing exact-scope overlay. Deliberately chain-blind: callers
174	   * addressing one scope's OWN contributions (its restrictions, its guards)
175	   * must not silently pick up an ancestor's — use {@link chainLayers} where
176	   * inheritance is the point.
177	   * @param scope - exact scope key; `undefined` denotes no overlay.
178	   * @returns the existing scoped layer, or `undefined` without creating one.
179	   */
180	  peek(scope: ScopeKey | undefined): L | undefined {
181	    if (scope === undefined) return undefined
182	    return this.scoped.get(scope)
183	  }
184	
185	  /**
186	   * Existing overlays along the scope's parent chain ({@link scopeChainOf}),
187	   * farthest ancestor first and the exact scope last, so a caller layering
188	   * them in order gives the nearest scope the final word.
189	   * @param scope - viewing scope, or `undefined` for no overlays.
190	   * @returns the existing layers, nearest last; absent overlays are skipped.
191	   */
192	  chainLayers(scope: ScopeKey | undefined): L[] {
193	    const layers: L[] = []
194	    for (const key of scopeChainOf(scope).reverse()) {
195	      const layer = this.scoped.get(key)
196	      if (layer !== undefined) layers.push(layer)
197	    }
198	    return layers
199	  }
200	
201	  /**
202	   * Materialize global named entries followed by scope-chain shadows,
203	   * farthest ancestor first, so the nearest scope's entry wins a name.
204	   * @param scope - viewing scope, or `undefined` for the global view.
205	   * @param pick - select the named table from a layer.
206	   * @returns an insertion-ordered effective map.
207	   */
208	  merge<V>(
209	    scope: ScopeKey | undefined,
210	    pick: (layer: L) => NamedEntries<V>,
211	  ): Map<string, V> {
212	    const merged = new Map(pick(this.global).entries())
213	    for (const layer of this.chainLayers(scope)) {
214	      for (const [name, value] of pick(layer).entries()) merged.set(name, value)
215	    }
216	    return merged
217	  }
218	
219	  /**
220	   * Attach one synchronous layer mutation to its registration context.
221	   * @param ctx - context that determines both scope visibility and effect ownership.
222	   * @param action - atomic mutation returning its synchronous undo.
223	   * @param options - Cordis effect label and optional change notification.
224	   * @returns the exact disposer returned by `ctx.effect()`.
225	   */
226	  effect(
227	    ctx: Context,
228	    action: (layer: L) => () => void,
229	    options: { label: string; notify?: boolean },
230	  ): () => void {
231	    const scope = scopeOf(ctx)
232	    const notify = options.notify ?? true
233	    const dispose = ctx.effect(function* (this: ScopedLayers<L>) {
234	      let layer: L
235	      let created = false
236	      if (scope === undefined) {
237	        layer = this.global
238	      } else {
239	        const existing = this.scoped.get(scope)
240	        if (existing === undefined) {
241	          layer = this.createLayer(scope)
242	          this.scoped.set(scope, layer)
243	          created = true
244	        } else {
245	          layer = existing
246	        }
247	      }
248	
249	      let undo: () => void
250	      try {
251	        undo = action(layer)
252	      } catch (error) {
253	        if (scope !== undefined && created && layer.isEmpty()) this.scoped.delete(scope)
254	        throw error
255	      }
256	
257	      yield () => {
258	        undo()
259	        if (scope !== undefined && layer.isEmpty()) this.scoped.delete(scope)
260	        if (notify) this.onChange()
261	      }
262	      if (notify) this.onChange()
263	    }.bind(this), options.label)
264	    // oxlint-disable-next-line typescript/no-misused-promises -- exact synchronous disposer preserves Cordis effect identity
265	    return dispose
266	  }
267	}
268

1	/**
2	 * Scoped-context primitive: mint a Cordis context that tags registrations with
3	 * an opaque identity and build routing-only event carriers for that identity.
4	 *
5	 * @module @deepseek-ai/dsh-scope
6	 */
7	
8	import type { Context, Fiber } from '@deepseek-ai/cordis'
9	import { Context as CordisContext } from '@deepseek-ai/cordis'
10	
11	export { AnonymousEntries, NamedEntries, ScopedLayers } from './store.ts'
12	export type { ScopeLayer } from './store.ts'
13	
14	/** An opaque, identity-compared scope key. */
15	export type ScopeKey = object
16	
17	/** Context tag written by {@link createScope}. */
18	const kScope = Symbol('dsh.scope')
19	
20	declare const ScopedBrand: unique symbol
21	
22	/**
23	 * A routing-only event receiver built by {@link scopeTarget}. The type
24	 * parameter records the subject type for dispatch checking; the carrier does
25	 * not expose the subject's properties. Event payloads carry the real subject.
26	 */
27	export type Scoped<T extends object> = object & { readonly [ScopedBrand]: T }
28	
29	/** The key associated with each carrier. Presence distinguishes an unkeyed carrier from a non-carrier. */
30	const carrierKeys = new WeakMap<object, ScopeKey | undefined>()
31	
32	/**
33	 * The enclosing scope of each key. One relation powers both directions of
34	 * scope nesting: registration views inherit DOWN the chain (a child scope
35	 * sees its ancestors' layers — {@link ScopedLayers}), and event admission
36	 * extends UP it (a listener tagged with an ancestor receives events dispatched
37	 * to a descendant key — {@link scopeTarget}).
38	 */
39	const scopeParents = new WeakMap<ScopeKey, ScopeKey>()
40	
41	/** The privileged handle to move one scope key's parent link. */
42	export interface ScopeParentBinding {
43	  /**
44	   * Re-link the bound key to a different parent, with the same cycle check as
45	   * the bind. Valid only while nothing produced under the old parent is
46	   * retained — the blank-session recompose contract, which the holder upholds
47	   * because this relation cannot see what a session logged.
48	   * @param parent - the new enclosing scope key.
49	   */
50	  rebind(parent: ScopeKey): void
51	}
52	
53	/** Cycle-checked write shared by the bind and every rebind. */
54	function linkScopeParent(key: ScopeKey, parent: ScopeKey): void {
55	  for (let cursor: ScopeKey | undefined = parent; cursor !== undefined; cursor = scopeParents.get(cursor)) {
56	    if (cursor === key) throw new Error('dsh-scope: scope parent link would form a cycle')
57	  }
58	  scopeParents.set(key, parent)
59	}

61	/**
62	 * Bind `parent` as `key`'s enclosing scope, once.
63	 *
64	 * A key that already has a parent throws: there is no open re-link path, so a
65	 * scope's ancestry cannot be moved by anyone but the original binder, who
66	 * alone receives the {@link ScopeParentBinding}. A link that would close a
67	 * cycle is rejected, because every chain consumer walks parents to the root.
68	 * @param key - the child scope key.
69	 * @param parent - its enclosing scope key.
70	 * @returns the binding that alone may re-link this key.
71	 */
72	export function bindScopeParent(key: ScopeKey, parent: ScopeKey): ScopeParentBinding {
73	  if (scopeParents.has(key)) {
74	    throw new Error('dsh-scope: scope key is already bound to a parent; re-linking requires the binding returned by the original bind')
75	  }
76	  linkScopeParent(key, parent)
77	  return {
78	    rebind(next: ScopeKey): void {
79	      linkScopeParent(key, next)
80	    },
81	  }
82	}

93	/**

96	 * @returns keys nearest-first: `[key, parent, grandparent, …]`.
97	 */
98	export function scopeChainOf(key: ScopeKey | undefined): ScopeKey[] {
99	  const chain: ScopeKey[] = []
100	  for (let cursor = key; cursor !== undefined; cursor = scopeParents.get(cursor)) chain.push(cursor)

104	/** A minted registration scope and its quiescent disposal boundaries. */
105	export interface Scope {
106	  /** Context through which scope-owned registrations are made. */
107	  ctx: Context
108	  /** Exact Cordis disposer, used when nesting this scope in an ordered composite effect. */
109	  rawDispose: () => Promise<void> | void

114	/** Follow a Cordis fiber through asynchronous teardown even if its raw disposer was already claimed. */
115	async function quiesceFiber(fiber: Fiber): Promise<void> {
116	  await Promise.resolve(fiber.dispose())
117	  while (fiber.inertia !== undefined) await fiber.inertia
118	}

120	/** Shared no-op plugin used as the backing scope fiber. */
121	function scope(): void {}

124	export interface CreateScopeOptions {
125	  /** Enclosing scope bound via {@link bindScopeParent} before the scope is usable; the binding stays internal. */
126	  parent?: ScopeKey
127	}

129	/**
130	 * Mint a scope under `ctx`. The scoped context inherits the minting plugin's
131	 * dependency API and owns every registration made through it.
132	 * @param ctx - active context whose dependency API the scope inherits.
133	 * @param key - opaque identity used for listener routing.
134	 * @param options - optional scope-chain placement.
135	 * @returns the scoped context and exact/shared disposal boundaries.
136	 */
137	export function createScope(ctx: Context, key: ScopeKey, options?: CreateScopeOptions): Scope {
138	  if (options?.parent !== undefined) bindScopeParent(key, options.parent)
139	  const fiber = ctx.plugin(scope)
140	  const scoped: Context = fiber.ctx.extend({ [kScope]: key })
141	  let disposing: Promise<void> | undefined
142	  return {
143	    ctx: scoped,
144	    rawDispose: fiber.dispose,
145	    dispose: () => (disposing ??= quiesceFiber(fiber)),
146	  }
147	}

149	/**
150	 * Read the nearest scope tag inherited by a context.
151	 * @param ctx - context to inspect.
152	 * @returns its scope key, or `undefined` for an unscoped context.
153	 */
154	export function scopeOf(ctx: Context): ScopeKey | undefined {
155	  return (ctx as Context & { [kScope]?: ScopeKey })[kScope]
156	}

158	/**
159	 * Build an opaque receiver that preserves the base filter, admits untagged
160	 * listeners globally, and admits tagged listeners for a matching key or any
161	 * of its ancestors ({@link bindScopeParent}): a listener owned by an enclosing
162	 * scope receives every descendant scope's events, which is what lets one
163	 * standing composition observe each of the agents composed under it. A tag
164	 * BELOW the dispatch key stays excluded — events flow up the chain, never
165	 * down.
166	 * @param base - subject or service whose existing Cordis filter is preserved.
167	 * @param key - routed scope identity, or `undefined` for an unscoped subject.
168	 * @returns a carrier whose subject remains available only through event arguments.
169	 */
170	export function scopeTarget<T extends object>(base: T, key: ScopeKey | undefined): Scoped<T> {
171	  const baseFilter = (base as { [CordisContext.filter]?: (ctx: Context) => boolean })[CordisContext.filter]
172	  const carrier = {
173	    [CordisContext.filter](ctx: Context): boolean {
174	      if (baseFilter !== undefined && !baseFilter.call(base, ctx)) return false
175	      const tag = scopeOf(ctx)
176	      if (tag === undefined) return true
177	      for (let cursor = key; cursor !== undefined; cursor = scopeParents.get(cursor)) {
178	        if (cursor === tag) return true
179	      }
180	      return false
181	    },
182	  }
183	  carrierKeys.set(carrier, key)
184	  return carrier as unknown as Scoped<T>
185	}

187	/**
188	 * Test whether a value is a scope carrier.
189	 * @param value - dispatch receiver to inspect.
190	 * @returns whether {@link scopeTarget} created it.
191	 */
192	export function isScopeCarrier(value: unknown): value is Scoped<object> {
193	  return typeof value === 'object' && value !== null && carrierKeys.has(value)
194	}
195	
196	/**
197	 * Read a carrier's routing key.
198	 * @param value - dispatch receiver to inspect.
199	 * @returns the carrier key, or `undefined` for an unkeyed/non-carrier value.
200	 */
201	export function carrierKeyOf(value: unknown): ScopeKey | undefined {
202	  if (!isScopeCarrier(value)) return undefined
203	  return carrierKeys.get(value)
204	}

18	 * No runtime invariant: the registry holds composition-time state mirrored from live seams through
19	 * effect-bound registrations; it owns no durable event stream or mutable relation a fold could check.
20	 */
21	const install: InvariantInstaller = () => {}
22	
23	/**
24	 * Register this package's invariant companion.
25	 * @param ctx - Cordis context carrying the invariant service.
26	 * @returns the installed registration's disposer after setup succeeds.
27	 */
28	export const apply = (ctx: Context): Promise<() => void> =>
29	  Promise.resolve(ctx.invariants.register(PACKAGE_NAME, install))
30	/* jscpd:ignore-end */

1	# @deepseek-ai/dsh-components
2	
3	English | [中文](README.zh.md)
4	
5	Component registry: the composition-time inventory of every addressable unit — a plugin, or a plugin-provided member such as a tool, skill, subagent provider, workflow, MCP server, context provider, preset, or composition — with its kind, provenance, lineage, membership, and the tool a model calls to reach it. The registry executes nothing. The [component-registry Agent Note](../../../.agents/notes/proposed/architecture/2026-09-01-component-registry-seam.md) owns the design rationale.
6	
7	## Config
8	
9	```yaml
10	- id: components
11	  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-components'
12	```
13	
14	The service takes no configuration; producers and consumers compose beside it.
15	
16	## Service contract
17	
18	`ctx.components.register(descriptor)` stores one `ComponentDescriptor` and returns the exact disposer that removes that registration and no later one under the same id; a duplicate id throws `ComponentError` with code `COMPONENT_DUPLICATE_ID`. Registrations are effects: a producer keeps the disposer under its own fiber so disposal removes the component. `get(id)` and `list(kind?)` return detached copies in registration order; a caller cannot mutate stored member lists through them.
19	
20	A descriptor carries a branded `ComponentId`, a `kind` from the merge-extensible `ComponentKindMap` (each producer declares its kind and detail type by declaration merging on `@deepseek-ai/dsh-components/types`; this package declares none), `name`, `description`, the owning package, `provenance` (`curated` or `synthesized`), an optional `lineage` parent id, optional `members` for compositions, an optional `invoke` pointer naming the existing tool and fixed arguments that reach the component, and kind-specific `detail`.
21	
22	## Extension points
23	
24	Producers are adapter packages that mirror one seam's live registry and follow that seam's own events; `@deepseek-ai/dsh-components-subagents` is the first. Consumers read the inventory: `@deepseek-ai/dsh-command-components` renders it for humans, and the verification, improvement, and oversight seams take component ids as the subject of certificates, scores, and audits.
25	
26	## Model Experience
27	
28	None, as the registry holds composition-time inventory and registers nothing model-facing; consumers own any rendered use.
29	
30	#### KV Cache effect
31	
32	None; the registry neither adds to nor changes any model request.
33	
34	## Known Limitations and Deferred Work
35	
36	- **Composition-time only** — the registry holds no durable record; promotion records and per-component evidence ride session events and the storage domain in the improvement seam's promotion slice.
37	- **No dispatch** — the `invoke` pointer is data for consumers; the `component_invoke` tool that follows it is a later Consumer.
38	- **Kinds arrive with producers** — a program with no adapter composed sees `ComponentKind` as `string` and an empty inventory.
39

A component is one addressable unit of a composition: a plugin, or a plugin-provided member such as a tool, skill, subagent provider, workflow, MCP server, context provider, preset, or composition. The [component-registry Agent Note](../../.agents/notes/proposed/architecture/2026-09-01-component-registry-seam.md) owns the design; this page records the exact fields from [`packages/components/components/src/types.ts`](../../packages/components/components/src/types.ts). 6 7 ## Descriptor 8 9 `ComponentId` is a [branded id](core.md#branded-ids) derived from the kind and the owning seam's stable name, never from mount order. Kinds are a merge-extensible map each producer package declares by declaration merging; the registry ships none. 10 11 ```ts type-equiv 12 /** One addressable unit of a composition. */ 13 interface ComponentDescriptor { 14 /** Stable identity across compositions. */ 15 readonly id: ComponentId 16 /** Declared kind. */ 17 readonly kind: K 18 /** Human-readable name. */ 19 readonly name: string 20 /** What the component does, stated for people and models. */ 21 readonly description: string 22 /** Package that produced the registration. */ 23 readonly owner: string 24 /** Curated by people or synthesized by an agent. */ 25 readonly provenance: ComponentProvenance 26 /** Component this one derived from, absent for roots. */ 27 readonly lineage?: ComponentId 28 /** Child components of a composition, absent for leaves. */ 29 readonly members?: readonly ComponentId[] 30 /** How a model reaches the component, absent for kinds without a callable route. */ 31 readonly invoke?: ComponentInvoke 32 /** Kind-specific detail. */ 33 readonly detail: ComponentDetail 34 } 35 ``` 36 37 ## Callable route 38 39 The invoke pointer names an existing tool and the arguments the component fixes; the model supplies the rest. The registry executes nothing. 40 41 ```ts type-equiv 42 /** The existing tool a model calls, with fixed arguments, to reach a component. */ 43 interface ComponentInvoke { 44 /** Registered tool name. */ 45 readonly tool: string 46 /** Arguments fixed by the component; the model supplies the rest. */ 47 readonly arguments?: Readonly> 48 } 49 ``` 50 51 52 53 54 55 ## Cordis API 56 57 Generated from source by `scripts/gen-cordis-catalog.ts` (verified fresh by `pnpm run verify-cordis-catalog` in doc-sync; regenerate with `pnpm run gen-cordis-catalog`) — this section is byte-identical in both language sides of the page. Signature blocks use a `ts cordis-catalog` fence and keep the original source JSDoc; dispatch modes are defined in the [primer](../cordis-primer.md#dispatch-modes), and the framework-inherited `ctx` API lives in [cordis-api/inherited.md](../cordis-api/inherited.md). 58 59 60 61 ### `ctx.components` — `ComponentRegistry` 62 63 Component registry (`ctx.components`): the composition-time inventory mirrored from live seams. 64 65 ```ts cordis-catalog 66 /** 67 * Register one component. Registrations are effects: the producer keeps the 68 * returned disposer under its own fiber so disposal removes the component. 69 * @param descriptor - complete component description. 70 * @returns the exact disposer that removes this registration and no later one under the same id. 71 * @throws {@link ComponentError} when the id is already registered. 72 */ 73 register(descriptor: ComponentDescriptor): () => void 74 75 /** 76 * Read one component. 77 * @param id - component identity. 78 * @returns a detached descriptor, or `undefined` when nothing is registered under the id. 79 */ 80 get(id: ComponentIdType): ComponentDescriptor | undefined 81 82 /** 83 * List components in registration order. 84 * @param kind - when given, only components of this kind. 85 * @returns detached descriptors. 86 */ 87 list(kind?: ComponentKind): ComponentDescriptor[] 88 ``` 89 90 Source: [`packages/components/components/src/index.ts:56`](../../packages/components/components/src/index.ts) 91 92
